summary_paragraph: A young woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia and tracheostomy was admitted for cough, blood-tinged sputum, chills, and increased trach secretions. She had recently been treated for Staphylococcus lugdunensis bacteremia and was on IV vancomycin. Workup revealed leukocytosis and acute kidney injury likely due to dehydration, which improved with IV fluids. CT chest showed centrilobular ground-glass opacities and bronchial wall thickening consistent with tracheobronchitis. Tracheoscopy revealed a mucosal abrasion in the left main bronchus, explaining the hemoptysis. She was treated with oral ciprofloxacin based on prior Pseudomonas sensitivity. Vancomycin dose was adjusted to 750 mg every 12 hours after a high trough level. Blood cultures remained negative. She improved clinically and was discharged home on continued IV vancomycin, ciprofloxacin, and home medications with plans for weekly lab monitoring.
